text.p: - Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek on Wednesday met representatives of parliamentary parties to discuss a common declaration on Slovenia joining NATO, which is due to be signed on Thursday.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan on Tuesday started a two-day visit to Norway.
- Slovenian drug producer Krka on Wednesday signed an agreement with Croatian Niva on the construction of Krka's new factory in Croatia. Krka said the investment would cost 10 million marks.
- Motorway company DARS said on Wednesday it will spend 75 billion tolars ($476.2 million) on the construction of motorways this year. The state will contribute 25 billion tolars.

- Cooperation between the two ruling coalition parties centre-left Liberal Democrats (LDS) and conservative People's Party is very good despite differences in their programmes, LDS's general secretary said on Wednesday.
- The number of applicants for 27 faculties at two Slovenian universities this year rose to 18,252 from 17,541 a year ago, the Ministry of Education said.
- Slovenian Privatisation Agency said that 1,373 companies have completed their privatisation, while 971 are still in progress.
- February average gross wages in Slovenia were 136,811 tolars ($868.6), 1.3 percent lower than in January and 14.1 percent higher than in the same month of 1996, the statistical office said.
